The stereochemistry of the product is influenced by the geometry of the alkene and the carbonyl group. The result of the reaction is the formation of a new carbon-carbon bond and a new stereocenter at the site of the allylic hydrogen, in which one of the substituents is going to be a hydroxyl group. Additionally, the reaction involves the change in the order of a C=C bond to a C-C bond, and a C=O bond to a C-O bond. 'ketones' and 'C-C double bonds' are gone, while an 'aliphatic hydroxyl' and a 'five-membered rings' are formed. A Carbon-Carbon bond is formed..
